review.title: Preamble: purposes of government
review.plain: Government exists to secure the body politic and let individuals enjoy their natural rights in safety; when it fails, the people have a right to alter it. The people of Massachusetts establish this Declaration of Rights and Frame of Government.
rights: the people have a right to alter the government
powers: do agree upon, ordain and establish the following Declaration of Rights, and Frame of Government

provisions.what: The end of the institution, maintenance, and administration of government, is to secure the existence of the body politic, to protect it, and to furnish the individuals who compose it with the power of enjoying in safety and tranquility their natural rights, and the blessings of life
whenever these great objects are not obtained, the people have a right to alter the government, and to take measures necessary for their safety, prosperity and happiness
conditions: whenever these great objects are not obtained

provisions.what: The body politic is formed by a voluntary association of individuals: it is a social compact, by which the whole people covenants with each citizen, and each citizen with the whole people, that all shall be governed by certain laws for the common good
It is the duty of the people, in framing a constitution of government, to provide for an equitable mode of making laws, as well as for an impartial interpretation, and a faithful execution of them
requires: to provide for an equitable mode of making laws, as well as for an impartial interpretation, and a faithful execution of them

provisions.what: We, the people of Massachusetts, do agree upon, ordain and establish the following Declaration of Rights, and Frame of Government, as the Constitution of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts

review.title: Natural rights of all people
review.plain: Annulled: This article said all men are born free and equal and have natural, essential and unalienable rights, including enjoying and defending their lives and liberties, acquiring and protecting property, and seeking safety and happiness. A note says it was annulled by Amendments, Art. CVI.
rights: the right of enjoying and defending their lives and liberties
that of acquiring, possessing, and protecting property
that of seeking and obtaining their safety and happiness

provisions.what: All men are born free and equal

All men have certain natural, essential, and unalienable rights; among which may be reckoned the right of enjoying and defending their lives and liberties; that of acquiring, possessing, and protecting property; in fine, that of seeking and obtaining their safety and happiness

review.title: Freedom of worship
review.plain: Worshipping the Supreme Being publicly and at stated seasons is the right and duty of all men in society. No subject shall be hurt, molested or restrained for worshipping God as his conscience dictates, or for his religious profession or sentiments, if he does not disturb the public peace or others' worship.
rights: for worshipping God in the manner and season most agreeable to the dictates of his own conscience
for his religious profession or sentiments
limits: no subject shall be hurt, molested, or restrained, in his person, liberty, or estate

provisions.what: It is the right as well as the duty of all men in society, publicly, and at stated seasons to worship the Supreme Being, the great Creator and Preserver of the universe
It is the duty of all men in society, publicly, and at stated seasons to worship the Supreme Being

no subject shall be hurt, molested, or restrained, in his person, liberty, or estate, for worshipping God in the manner and season most agreeable to the dictates of his own conscience; or for his religious profession or sentiments
forbids: hurting, molesting, or restraining a subject in his person, liberty, or estate, for worshipping God in the manner and season most agreeable to the dictates of his own conscience
or for his religious profession or sentiments
exceptions: provided he doth not disturb the public peace, or obstruct others in their religious worship

review.title: Public worship and religious teachers
review.plain: Annulled: A bracketed note says Article XI of the Amendments was substituted for this article. It provided that the legislature shall require towns, parishes and religious societies to provide for public worship and Protestant teachers, could enjoin attendance on their instruction, and that no sect shall be subordinated to another by law.

provisions.what: the people of this commonwealth have a right to invest their legislature with power to authorize and require the several towns, parishes, precincts, and other bodies politic, or religious societies, to make suitable provision, at their own expense, for the institution of the public worship of God, and for the support and maintenance of public Protestant teachers of piety, religion and morality
provisions.holder: The people of this commonwealth; their legislature
conditions: in all cases where such provision shall not be made voluntarily
changedBy: Art. XI of the Amendments substituted for this.

provisions.what: the legislature shall, from time to time, authorize and require, the several towns, parishes, precincts, and other bodies politic, or religious societies, to make suitable provision, at their own expense, for the institution of the public worship of God, and for the support and maintenance of public Protestant teachers of piety, religion and morality
conditions: in all cases where such provision shall not be made voluntarily
changedBy: Art. XI of the Amendments substituted for this.

provisions.what: the people of this commonwealth do invest their legislature with authority to enjoin upon all the subjects an attendance upon the instructions of the public teachers aforesaid, at stated times and seasons
conditions: if there be any on whose instructions they can conscientiously and conveniently attend
changedBy: Art. XI of the Amendments substituted for this.

provisions.what: the several towns, parishes, precincts, and other bodies politic, or religious societies, shall, at all times, have the exclusive right of electing their public teachers, and of contracting with them for their support and maintenance
provisions.holder: The several towns, parishes, precincts, and other bodies politic, or religious societies
changedBy: Art. XI of the Amendments substituted for this.

provisions.what: all moneys paid by the subject to the support of public worship, and of the public teachers aforesaid, shall, if he require it, be uniformly applied to the support of the public teacher or teachers of his own religious sect or denomination
conditions: provided there be any on whose instructions he attends
exceptions: otherwise it may be paid towards the support of the teacher or teachers of the parish or precinct in which the said moneys are raised
changedBy: Art. XI of the Amendments substituted for this.

provisions.what: every denomination of Christians, demeaning themselves peaceably, and as good subjects of the commonwealth, shall be equally under the protection of the law
conditions: demeaning themselves peaceably, and as good subjects of the commonwealth
changedBy: Art. XI of the Amendments substituted for this.

provisions.what: no subordination of any one sect or denomination to another shall ever be established by law
forbids: establishing by law the subordination of any one sect or denomination to another
changedBy: Art. XI of the Amendments substituted for this.

review.title: Right of self-government
review.plain: The people of the commonwealth have the sole and exclusive right to govern themselves as a free, sovereign and independent state, and keep every power, jurisdiction and right not expressly delegated by them to the United States of America in Congress assembled.
rights: the sole and exclusive right of governing themselves, as a free, sovereign, and independent state
exercise and enjoy every power, jurisdiction, and right

provisions.what: The people of this commonwealth have the sole and exclusive right of governing themselves, as a free, sovereign, and independent state

The people of this commonwealth do, and forever hereafter shall, exercise and enjoy every power, jurisdiction, and right, which is not, or may not hereafter, be by them expressly delegated to the United States of America in Congress assembled
exceptions: which is not, or may not hereafter, be by them expressly delegated to the United States of America in Congress assembled

review.title: Officials accountable to the people
review.plain: All power resides originally in the people and is derived from them, so the magistrates and officers of government, whether legislative, executive or judicial, are their substitutes and agents and are at all times accountable to them.
powers: All power residing originally in the people

provisions.what: All power residing originally in the people, and being derived from them, the several magistrates and officers of government, vested with authority, whether legislative, executive, or judicial, are their substitutes and agents
the several magistrates and officers of government are at all times accountable to them
provisions.binds: The several magistrates and officers of government, whether legislative, executive, or judicial

review.title: No hereditary privileges
review.plain: No man, corporation or association has any title to advantages or exclusive privileges apart from the community except from services rendered to the public. That title is not hereditary, so a man born a magistrate, lawgiver or judge is absurd and unnatural.
limits: have any other title to obtain advantages, or particular and exclusive privileges, distinct from those of the community
neither hereditary, nor transmissible to children, or descendants, or relations by blood

provisions.what: No man, nor corporation, or association of men, have any other title to obtain advantages, or particular and exclusive privileges, distinct from those of the community, than what arises from the consideration of services rendered to the public
provisions.binds: No man, nor corporation, or association of men
exceptions: what arises from the consideration of services rendered to the public

provisions.what: this title being in nature neither hereditary, nor transmissible to children, or descendants, or relations by blood, the idea of a man born a magistrate, lawgiver, or judge, is absurd and unnatural

review.title: Purpose of government; right to change it
review.plain: Government is instituted for the common good and the protection, safety, prosperity and happiness of the people, not for the profit of any one man, family or class. The people alone have an unalienable right to institute government and to reform, alter or totally change it.
rights: an incontestable, unalienable, and indefeasible right to institute government
to reform, alter, or totally change the same
limits: not for the profit, honor, or private interest of any one man, family, or class of men

provisions.what: Government is instituted for the common good; for the protection, safety, prosperity and happiness of the people; and not for the profit, honor, or private interest of any one man, family, or class of men
the people alone have an incontestable, unalienable, and indefeasible right to institute government; and to reform, alter, or totally change the same
conditions: when their protection, safety, prosperity and happiness require it

review.title: Right to remove officers by election
review.plain: To keep those in authority from becoming oppressors, the people have a right, at periods and in a manner set by their frame of government, to return public officers to private life and to fill vacancies by regular elections and appointments.
rights: to cause their public officers to return to private life
to fill up vacant places by certain and regular elections and appointments

provisions.what: the people have a right to cause their public officers to return to private life; and to fill up vacant places by certain and regular elections and appointments
conditions: at such periods and in such manner as they shall establish by their frame of government

review.title: Free elections and equal right to vote
review.plain: All elections ought to be free, and all inhabitants of the commonwealth who have the qualifications set by the frame of government have an equal right to elect officers and to be elected to public employments.
rights: an equal right to elect officers, and to be elected, for public employments

provisions.what: All elections ought to be free
requires: All elections ought to be free

provisions.what: all the inhabitants of this commonwealth have an equal right to elect officers, and to be elected, for public employments
provisions.holder: All the inhabitants of this commonwealth
conditions: having such qualifications as they shall establish by their frame of government

review.title: Protection of life, liberty and property
review.plain: Each individual has a right to be protected in life, liberty and property under standing laws, and must contribute his share to that protection. No property may be taken or applied to public uses without his consent or that of the representative body, and property appropriated to public uses requires reasonable compensation.
rights: a right to be protected by it in the enjoyment of his life, liberty and property
he shall receive a reasonable compensation therefor
limits: no part of the property of any individual can, with justice, be taken from him, or applied to public uses
are not controllable by any other laws

provisions.what: Each individual of the society has a right to be protected by it in the enjoyment of his life, liberty and property, according to standing laws
He is obliged to contribute his share to the expense of this protection; to give his personal service, or an equivalent, when necessary
requires: to contribute his share to the expense of this protection
to give his personal service, or an equivalent, when necessary

provisions.what: no part of the property of any individual can, with justice, be taken from him, or applied to public uses, without his own consent, or that of the representative body of the people
forbids: taking the property of any individual from him, or applying it to public uses, without his own consent, or that of the representative body of the people

provisions.what: the people of this commonwealth are not controllable by any other laws than those to which their constitutional representative body have given their consent
exceptions: those to which their constitutional representative body have given their consent

provisions.what: whenever the public exigencies require that the property of any individual should be appropriated to public uses, he shall receive a reasonable compensation therefor
provisions.holder: The individual whose property is appropriated
conditions: whenever the public exigencies require that the property of any individual should be appropriated to public uses

review.title: Right to a remedy in the laws
review.plain: Every subject ought to find a certain remedy in the laws for injuries to his person, property or character, and to obtain right and justice freely, completely, promptly and without delay, conformably to the laws.
rights: ought to find a certain remedy, by having recourse to the laws
obtain right and justice freely, and without being obliged to purchase it

provisions.what: Every subject of the commonwealth ought to find a certain remedy, by having recourse to the laws, for all injuries or wrongs which he may receive in his person, property, or character
He ought to obtain right and justice freely, and without being obliged to purchase it; completely, and without any denial; promptly, and without delay; conformably to the laws

review.title: Rights of the accused; trial by jury
review.plain: No subject shall answer for a crime until it is fully described to him, or be compelled to accuse himself. He may produce favorable proofs, meet witnesses face to face and be fully heard. No one may be deprived of life, liberty or property but by judgment of his peers or the law of the land.
rights: a right to produce all proofs, that may be favorable to him
to meet the witnesses against him face to face
to be fully heard in his defense by himself, or his council at his election
limits: No subject shall be held to answer for any crimes or offence
be compelled to accuse, or furnish evidence against himself
no subject shall be arrested, imprisoned, despoiled, or deprived of his property, immunities, or privileges
the legislature shall not make any law, that shall subject any person to a capital or infamous punishment

provisions.what: No subject shall be held to answer for any crimes or offence, until the same is fully and plainly, substantially and formally, described to him
forbids: holding a subject to answer for any crimes or offence until the same is fully and plainly, substantially and formally, described to him

provisions.what: No subject shall be compelled to accuse, or furnish evidence against himself
forbids: compelling a subject to accuse, or furnish evidence against himself

provisions.what: every subject shall have a right to produce all proofs, that may be favorable to him; to meet the witnesses against him face to face, and to be fully heard in his defense by himself, or his council at his election

no subject shall be arrested, imprisoned, despoiled, or deprived of his property, immunities, or privileges, put out of the protection of the law, exiled, or deprived of his life, liberty, or estate, but by the judgment of his peers, or the law of the land
forbids: arresting, imprisoning, despoiling, or depriving a subject of his property, immunities, or privileges, putting him out of the protection of the law, exiling him, or depriving him of his life, liberty, or estate
exceptions: but by the judgment of his peers, or the law of the land

provisions.what: the legislature shall not make any law, that shall subject any person to a capital or infamous punishment, without trial by jury
forbids: making any law that shall subject any person to a capital or infamous punishment without trial by jury
exceptions: excepting for the government of the army and navy

review.title: Facts tried in the vicinity
review.plain: In criminal prosecutions, verifying the facts in the vicinity where they happen is one of the greatest securities of the citizen's life, liberty and property.

provisions.what: In criminal prosecutions, the verification of facts in the vicinity where they happen, is one of the greatest securities of the life, liberty, and property of the citizen

review.title: Searches, seizures and warrants
review.plain: Every subject has a right to be secure from unreasonable searches and seizures. Warrants are contrary to this right unless supported by oath or affirmation and specially designating the persons or objects, and no warrant ought to be issued except in cases and with formalities the laws prescribe.
rights: a right to be secure from all unreasonable searches, and seizures, of his person, his houses, his papers, and all his possessions
limits: All warrants, therefore, are contrary to this right
no warrant ought to be issued

provisions.what: Every subject has a right to be secure from all unreasonable searches, and seizures, of his person, his houses, his papers, and all his possessions

All warrants are contrary to this right, if the cause or foundation of them be not previously supported by oath or affirmation; and if the order in the warrant to a civil officer, to make search in suspected places, or to arrest one or more suspected persons, or to seize their property, be not accompanied with a special designation of the persons or objects of search, arrest, or seizure
requires: the cause or foundation of them be previously supported by oath or affirmation
the order in the warrant be accompanied with a special designation of the persons or objects of search, arrest, or seizure

provisions.what: no warrant ought to be issued but in cases, and with the formalities prescribed by the laws
exceptions: in cases, and with the formalities prescribed by the laws

review.title: Right to a jury in civil cases
review.plain: In controversies about property and suits between persons, the parties have a right to a jury trial, which shall be held sacred, except where other practice was used before, and unless the legislature finds it necessary to alter it in high-seas and mariners' wages cases.
rights: the parties have a right to a trial by jury
limits: this method of procedure shall be held sacred

provisions.what: In all controversies concerning property, and in all suits between two or more persons, the parties have a right to a trial by jury
conditions: In all controversies concerning property, and in all suits between two or more persons
exceptions: except in cases in which it has heretofore been otherways used and practiced

provisions.what: this method of procedure shall be held sacred
exceptions: unless, in causes arising on the high seas, and such as relate to mariners' wages, the legislature shall hereafter find it necessary to alter it

review.title: Liberty of the press
review.plain: Annulled: This article, printed in brackets as superseded, said the liberty of the press is essential to the security of freedom and ought not to be restrained in this commonwealth. A bracketed note in the text says it was annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LXXVII.

provisions.what: The liberty of the press is essential to the security of freedom in a state: it ought not, therefore, to be restrained in this commonwealth
forbids: restraining the liberty of the press in this commonwealth
changedBy: Annulled and superseded by Amendments, Art. LXXVII.

review.title: Right to bear arms; civilian control of military
review.plain: The people have a right to keep and bear arms for the common defence. Because armies in peacetime are dangerous to liberty, they ought not to be maintained without the legislature's consent, and the military shall always be subordinate to and governed by the civil authority.
rights: The people have a right to keep and to bear arms for the common defence
limits: ought not to be maintained without the consent of the legislature
the military power shall always be held in an exact subordination to the civil authority

provisions.what: The people have a right to keep and to bear arms for the common defence
in time of peace, armies ought not to be maintained without the consent of the legislature
forbids: maintaining armies in time of peace without the consent of the legislature

provisions.what: the military power shall always be held in an exact subordination to the civil authority, and be governed by it
requires: the military power shall always be held in an exact subordination to the civil authority, and be governed by it

review.title: Adherence to fundamental principles
review.plain: Frequent recurrence to the constitution's fundamental principles and to piety, justice, moderation, temperance, industry and frugality is necessary to a free government. The people ought to heed these in choosing officers and have a right to require lawgivers and magistrates to observe them.
rights: a right to require of their lawgivers and magistrates, an exact and constant observance of them

provisions.what: A frequent recurrence to the fundamental principles of the constitution, and a constant adherence to those of piety, justice, moderation, temperance, industry, and frugality, are absolutely necessary to preserve the advantages of liberty, and to maintain a free government
The people ought to have a particular attention to all those principles, in the choice of their officers and representatives

they have a right to require of their lawgivers and magistrates, an exact and constant observance of them, in the formation and execution of the laws necessary for the good administration of the commonwealth

review.title: Right to assemble, instruct and petition
review.plain: The people have a right, in an orderly and peaceable manner, to assemble to consult on the common good, to give instructions to their representatives, and to ask the legislative body, by addresses, petitions or remonstrances, for redress of wrongs and grievances.
rights: to assemble to consult upon the common good
give instructions to their representatives
to request of the legislative body, by the way of addresses, petitions, or remonstrances, redress of the wrongs done them

provisions.what: The people have a right to assemble to consult upon the common good; give instructions to their representatives, and to request of the legislative body, by the way of addresses, petitions, or remonstrances, redress of the wrongs done them, and of the grievances they suffer
conditions: in an orderly and peaceable manner
